Call highlights (from our notes):
- Primary workload: real-time summarization of customer support transcripts (tokenized on our side).
- Latency SLOs: 95th pct latency <= 350ms for single-turn streaming responses (partial tokens streamed), and <= 180ms p50 for short non-streaming generative calls.
- Throughput/concurrency: expected steady-state concurrency 40–60 concurrent users during peak; bursts to 150 for a few minutes. Estimated sustained tokens/sec ~ 12k–18k.
- Streaming: yes — partial response streaming required (must start sending tokens within ~120ms of generate start).
- Budget sensitivity: want orders-of-magnitude decrease vs current hosted provider; looking for cost levers to hit SLOs without overprovisioning.

Suggested next steps:
1) Engineering baseline: Dylan to review sample traffic CSV you sent (attached) and propose initial infra profile (GPU type + expected instance count) and batching targets.
2) Technical deep-dive: 30m with Dylan + Priyom to discuss quantization and caching tradeoffs.
3) POC plan: 2-week POC with ~50 concurrent users, streaming enabled, and telemetry capture (latency percentiles, token costs).

Attachments: redwood-slo-cheatsheet.pdf (overview of cost/perf levers), please also see your uploaded file (orion-current-load.csv) which you shared in the call.

Samir — thanks for the detail. Quick technical response ahead of the deep-dive with some concrete levers and ballpark impacts based on similar POCs we've run. High level: continuous batching + prefix/KV caching + targeted quantization + model variant selection tend to be the most impactful levers for streaming-heavy summarization.

Short answers to your questions:
1) Continuous batching: for a mixed-size streaming workload like yours, continuous batching typically reduces per-token compute by ~25–45% compared to one-request-per-call. Improvements depend on request size distribution and tail-latency guards; with aggressive batching and adaptive timeouts we often hit ~30–35% cost reduction without harming first-byte latency if coupled with prioritized small-request fast paths.

2) Quantization profiles:
- 8-bit (int8) quantization: strong cost wins, minimal quality degradation for many decoder-only models. Works well with KV cache.
- 4-bit (nf4 or q4_0/q4_k_m): larger speedups, but some models show small quality regressions on summarization; still often within your ~2% F1 tolerance depending on model.
- Mixed: keep embeddings/attention ops at 8-bit, quantize feed-forward to 4-bit for best tradeoff. We'll test both q8 and q4 profiles in POC.

3) Quality risk: some drop is possible with aggressive 4-bit quantization; we recommend a small eval harness (held-out prompts) to measure regression. For your POC we can run a gated rollout: q8 -> q4-mixed on a sample of traffic and compare NLG metrics and human spot checks.

Other levers & config suggestions:
- Prefix/KV caching: since summarization often reuses system prompts and conversation prefixes, caching KV for common prefixes can cut repeated compute substantially (20–50% for repeated flows).
- Fast-path small-request routing: route sub-150-token requests to low-latency nodes with smaller batch windows to hit first-byte targets.
- Model variants: test 7B fine-tuned baseline vs a quantized 13B distilled variant — occasionally the 13B-distilled quantized model matches quality with similar latency once quantized and pipelined. We'll include that comparison in the POC.
- Instance/GPU selection: for streaming low-p99, we prefer A100/RTX-class with optimized kernels; we can also evaluate multi-instance sharding for high-concurrency.

Ballpark expected outcomes for POC (given your profile):
- First-token latency improvement: from current ~200–300ms to ~80–150ms for most traffic using small-request fast paths + continuous batching.
- Cost reduction: 25–55% per-token cost reduction combining batching + quantization + caching (numbers range depending on model and quantization aggressiveness).
- Quality: aim to keep within your 2% F1 target with staged quantization/testing.

I'll prepare a short test matrix for Mon's call: q8 vs q4-mixed, caching on/off, model A (7B-finetuned) vs model B (13B-distilled-quant). Also will bring sample kernel-level latency estimates for the GPUs we propose.

Happy to walk through the matrix Monday — 10:00 PT works for me.
